title: 2016 AMC 10B Problem 18
statement: In how many ways can \(345\) be written as the sum of an increasing sequence of two or more consecutive positive integers?

solutions.text:
Suppose the sequence has length \(s\) and first term \(x\). Then \[345=s\left(x+\frac{s-1}{2}\right),\] or \[s(2x+s-1)=690.\]

Thus \(s\) must be a divisor of \(690\), with \(x=\frac{\frac{690}{s}-s+1}{2}\) a positive integer. Checking the possible divisor lengths gives \[s=2,3,5,6,10,15,23.\] These are the only lengths that keep \(x\) positive and integral.

Therefore there are \(7\) representations.

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: Check factor lengths that give positive integer \(x\)
